description.purpose: The generation ledger of the keeper: one row per session, that is, per channel generation. It answers exactly two questions -- which generation is a channel currently in, and when did that channel last speak -- and holds nothing else.
description.use_when: One per session-keeper hive. Both code cells of the hive write here and nowhere else; code cells own no state, so all of it lives in this store.
description.not_in_scope: No conversation turns, no tool rounds, no memory: what was said belongs to the collector's window and to the memory hive. No deletes -- a closed generation keeps its row, which is what makes the close idempotent and the history readable.
description.emits_meaning: messages[]: one tool_result per op. hop.operation drives the two passes, hop.rows_affected carries the guard signal of the close: a guarded update that affected 0 rows means this generation was already sealed and the emission is terminal.
description.consumes_meaning: messages[]: tool_call turns with store-native args. Which pass a reply belongs to is carried by context.store_origin ('keeper-stamp' / 'keeper-close'), the step by context.ses_phase, both promoted by the edge that sent the op.
examples: {operation: select, table: sessions, columns: [...], where: {channel, closed: 0}, order_by: [{col: 'opened_at', dir: 'desc'}], limit: 1} -> the generation a turn belongs to
{operation: update, table: sessions, set: {last_seen}, where: {session_id, closed: 0}} -> the channel is alive, the idle clock restarts
{operation: update, table: sessions, set: {closed: 1, closed_at}, where: {session_id, closed: 0}} -> rows_affected 1 means this pass owns the close and emits the close request
